statement: Washington levies no corporate net-income tax; instead most businesses in the state owe the business and occupation (B&O) tax under RCW 82.04, a gross-receipts tax calculated on the total value of products sold or the total income the business earns with no deduction for the costs of doing business, at a rate set by the business's B&O classification (more than 50 classifications exist), reported and paid on the excise tax return through the Department of Revenue's My DOR system.
caveat: A business performing several activities can owe under several classifications at once; the small business B&O credit, the multiple activities tax credit, and city-level B&O taxes materially change what is owed and are not carded here. Registration happens through the state business license application. This repo does not compute the tax.
reviewer: Lane editorial review (state process variants wave 2026-10-22); independent domain expert review pending
